lines.text: Some say the world will end in fire,
lines.meaning: Some people believe the world will be destroyed by *fire* — here, a symbol of desire and greed.
Others believe it will end in *ice* — a symbol of hatred and coldness.

narration: Let us read the first two lines of the poem together, slowly. {{b1.1.1}} Some say the world will end in fire. Listen to how calm the poet sounds while talking about the end of the world. {{b1.1.2}} What does he mean? Some people believe the world will be destroyed by fire. But this is not only real fire. Fire here is a symbol of desire, of greed, of wanting more and more. {{b1.2.1}} Now the second line: Some say in ice. Notice how short it is. Just four words. {{b1.2.2}} Other people believe the world will end in ice. And ice, too, is a symbol. It stands for hatred, for coldness between people, for not caring. So in just two lines, the poet has set up two big ideas. Can you guess which one he will choose?
